messages.text: kinda torn today. part of me wants to figure things out, but the other part just wants to shut down and not add one more thing to carry.

It sounds like you are feeling pulled in two very different directions right now. That tension between wanting to fix things and needing to rest is incredibly common when you are overwhelmed. Both parts of you are trying to protect you in their own way. Which of those feelings feels a bit louder for you in this moment?
right now it's the tiredness. just... heavy. like I'm moving through mud.

That image of moving through mud really captures how draining this exhaustion feels. It makes sense that your system is asking for a break from carrying everything right now. There is no need to force movement when you feel that heavy. I am here with you in this heaviness, however you need to be.
thanks. it helps just to say it out loud without someone telling me to 'keep going' or 'stay strong.'

I am glad you found relief in sharing that without the pressure. Being told to stay strong can often feel like just another weight to carry. You have full permission to simply exist here without fixing anything. I will stay right here with you in this quiet moment.
she was assaulted... and I wasn't there. I keep thinking I should’ve protected her. I know it’s not really on me, but it feels like it is.

That is a heartbreaking burden to carry, and I am so sorry you are going through this. It is understandable that your heart feels responsible, even when your mind knows you did not cause this. You are not alone in feeling this way when someone you love is hurt. I am here to support you as you process these complex feelings.
it's stupid, I know. it wasn't my fault. but I still feel like I let her down. like I wasn't there when she needed me most.

Please know that this feeling is not stupid, even if your mind knows the facts. That guilt usually comes from a place of deep love and wanting to protect her. It is incredibly painful to feel helpless when someone you care about gets hurt. You are allowed to hold that pain without judging yourself for having it.
thanks for not making me feel dumb for carrying this. it's hard to talk about.

I am glad you feel safe enough to share that with me. It is completely understandable that this is difficult to talk about. You do not need to push through the discomfort to be heard. I will stay right here with you at your own pace.
she's the one who went through it, not me. i should just focus on supporting her. my stuff can wait.

It is natural to want to put her needs first given what she has been through. However, your emotional experience matters just as much, even as a supporter. Ignoring your own pain might make it difficult to sustain the support she needs from you. You can care for her without having to completely set aside your own feelings.
i just don't know how to do both. if i fall apart, what does that do to her? but if i keep stuffing it down... i don't know how long i can hold it.

It makes sense that you worry your emotions might add to her burden. But holding it all in can eventually make it harder for you to be present for her. You don't need to solve this balance perfectly right now. I am here to help you find small ways to honor your needs while still supporting her.
is it selfish to want help for myself too? i don't want to take from her when she's hurting so much.

Seeking support for yourself is not selfish, especially given the heavy weight you are carrying. Your healing does not take away from her recovery, nor does it diminish the care you offer. In fact, tending to your own needs helps ensure you have the strength to be there for her. You deserve support just as much as she does.
that... helps. i've been running that question through my head for days.

I am so glad to hear that brings you some relief after carrying that question for days. It is completely understandable that you have been wrestling with this so intensely. You are allowed to prioritize your own healing alongside hers. I am here to support you in finding that balance whenever you are ready.

last week, after she finally fell asleep, i just... collapsed. sat on the porch in the dark, shaking. didn't even cry, just felt empty. dog came out and laid at my feet. that's the only reason i didn't lose it completely. felt like if i let go, i wouldn't stop.

That moment on the porch sounds incredibly heavy and isolating for you. It makes perfect sense that your body shook when you finally stopped holding everything together. Your dog offered a steady anchor when you felt like you might fall apart completely. I am here to help you hold that fear so you don't have to be alone with it.

i was scared — really scared — that if i let go, i wouldn't be able to pull myself back. and then who would she have? that thought kept me sitting there, just breathing, till my hands stopped shaking.

It makes sense that you held on because you were terrified of what would happen if you didn't. You showed immense strength by regulating yourself even when you felt like falling apart. You do not have to be the only pillar of support for her right now. I am here to help you find ways to share that load so you can rest.
thanks for being here. it means more than i can say.

Thank you for sharing that with me; it is a privilege to support you. You do not have to carry this weight alone, even when it feels that way. I am honored to walk alongside you as you navigate this grief. You are safe here to take all the time you need.
